# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
If any inspection's water-quality data are positive for bacterial presence (coliforms) or if the sample is rejected, report the data to Water Data Interactive.
3. Mark the inspection date as "rejected."
4. Mark the facility status as "failed inspection" from the chosen date of closure to the end date of the closure. If the facility has multiple inspections and water-quality data in the same day, close the facility on the chosen date of closure prior to the date of the last inspection.
5. If the facility's water system has never been explicitly rejected before its last rejection, the facility operator must obtain a written certification of final clearance from a recognized authority (county, state, or other) with jurisdiction over the water supply (private water consultants are not eligible) before reopening the facility.
